newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FINEMORE TO WRITE DOWN A$2.1 MILLION.
newsitem.headline: FINEMORE TO WRITE DOWN A$2.1 MILLION.

text.p: Transport contractor Finemore Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it would write down A$2.16 million in booked goodwill in its 1996/97 results following the unexpected cancellation of a longterm cartage arrangement.

Finemore said the arrangement between CSR Timbers, a unit of CSR Ltd, and Finemore subsidiary C.J. Dean, managed by the privately owned transport giant Linfox, was cancelled last week with only six days notice.
Finemore managing director Ron Finemore said he was extemely disappointed the contract had been terminated and with such short notice.

"While we intend to take on other business which will go a long way towards offsetting the loss of this revenue, we have decided to realistically write off the full proportion of goodwill which represents the CSR Timbers business acquired in 1994," he said in a statement.

Finemore said the company had sold, for an undisclosed small profit over book value, its poorly performing Queensland Forest Products division and its contracts with CSR Timbers in south-east Queensland.

"We had tried unsuccessfully for some time to turn this operation around however we were unable to obtain contracted price increases from the customer over the last few years," he said. "It was therefore essential that we removed this loss-making contract," he said.
Finemore reported a net profit of A$9.2 million for the year to June 30, 1996, up from A$8.65 million a year earlier.
The shares closed at A$3.40 on Wednesday, down nine cents on the day.
